unit: freshman-math / P03_1 — Project 3: Somebody Is 2.7 Kilometres Away
note: One image, and it is not a downloaded map — it is generated from OpenStreetMap data by build-hoi-an-map.py, which sits beside it. The script is NOT part of the site build (nothing imports it and Vite never sees it); it is kept so the map can be rebuilt, re-scaled or re-anchored without guesswork. It needs a network connection and caches the Overpass responses next to itself.

images.usage: The whole of Project 3: the projected slides, the solution widget's base layer, and the printed handout (homework/alg13p3). One file for all three, so the map on the desk is the map on the wall.
images.frame: Bottom-left corner of the frame is longitude 108.316231 E, latitude 15.873640 N. The frame is 6400 m wide by 3600 m tall, rendered at 0.2 px per metre and then rasterised at 2x, so the file is 2560 x 1440 px.
images.projection: Local equirectangular about the frame's centre latitude (15.88992 N): 110600 m per degree of latitude, 111320 * cos(15.88992) = 107065 m per degree of longitude. Over 6.4 km the error against a proper geodesic is a few metres — far inside a pencil line. Crucially the scale is the SAME on both axes, which is what makes a circle of constant distance draw as a circle rather than an ellipse.
images.scale: Printed at 25.6 cm wide the map is exactly 1 cm = 250 m, so 1 km = 4 cm and the 2.7 km reading is a 10.8 cm radius. The scale bar drawn on the map is 200 px = 1 km and is the authority: if the sheet is ever printed at a different width, students measure off the bar and the arithmetic still works.
images.anchors: A Japanese Bridge (15.87712, 108.32601) at px (209.4, 643.0); B Tra Que Herb Village (15.90271, 108.33602) at px (423.7, 77.0); C Cua Dai Beach (15.89806, 108.36623) at px (1070.6, 179.8). All three are real OSM features at their real positions — nothing has been nudged to make the numbers work.
images.answer: The target is the cafe named Classic Coffee (15.89282, 108.34518) at px (619.9, 295.7). True distances 2688.4 m, 1469.1 m and 2327.1 m, which round to the 2.7 / 1.5 / 2.3 km the app reports. Do not mark it on the map.
